title: Money in integer cents
when: The app adds prices, applies discounts or taxes, splits bills or totals invoices, and results like 0.1 + 0.2 must never appear.
prompt:
Goal: All money stored and computed as integer minor units, with explicit rounding and allocation that always adds up.
Steps:
1. Store { amountCents: 1999, currency: "BRL" }; get the minor digits per currency from Intl.NumberFormat(...).resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits.
2. Parse typed amounts as text: split on the decimal symbol, build cents from the whole and fraction parts, reject extra decimals.
3. Rates and quantities: Math.round(cents * rate) with one rounding rule (half up or half even), once per line.
4. Taxes and discounts per line, rounded per line, then summed; note the rule in a comment.
5. Split among n: everyone gets Math.floor(total / n) and the remainder goes one cent at a time to the first parts.
6. Format only for display from cents / 100; switch to BigInt beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
Quality bar:
- Totals equal the sum of displayed lines.
- Splits never lose or invent a cent.
- Tests cover 0.1 plus 0.2, half rounding and remainders.
Pitfalls:
- Floats for money anywhere in the pipeline.
- Number(input) * 100, which turns 19.99 into 1998.9999.
- Rounding at several steps of one calculation.
Verify:
- [ ] No float money in storage.
- [ ] Allocation sums to the total in tests.
- [ ] One rounding helper.
- [ ] Formatting only at display.
Output: js/money.js exporting parseMoney, applyRate, allocate and formatMoney, plus tests.

examples.input: dividir a conta de R$ 100,00 entre 3 pessoas
examples.output: allocate(10000, 3) -> [3334, 3333, 3333], totals in cents, formatted only for display
